mainTopic: The indispensable details of the מילואים, and the order in which משה dressed אהרן and his sons
overview: The גמרא continues discussing which details of the מילואים, the seven-day inauguration of the כהנים, are indispensable (מעכב). It asks how we know that details written only in the fulfillment section in ספר ויקרא are also indispensable. Three אמוראים give three sources: a גזירה שוה from 'פתח', the phrase 'ושמרתם את משמרת ה׳', and the phrase 'כי כן צויתי'. That last phrase leads to a ברייתא explaining three similar 'command' phrases connected to eating the offering in אנינות. Next, רבי יוסי בר חנינא teaches that the מכנסים and the עשירית האיפה are included through the word 'וזה', and the גמרא finds a גזירה שוה of 'זה' for the עשירית האיפה. רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, adds that even reading the פרשה aloud was מעכב. Finally, the גמרא asks in what order משה dressed אהרן and his sons, and justifies the question as a way to understand the פסוקים. אביי narrows the dispute to the אבנט, and the גמרא challenges the 'together' view from the verses in ויקרא; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: What about details not written in this section?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that details written in the ספר שמות section are indispensable, and asks for the source for details written only in ספר ויקרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A detail that is written in this section is indispensable. But a detail that is not written in this section, how do we know it is indispensable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא grants that the details written in the command section of the מילואים are indispensable. Then it asks for the source for the details that appear only in the fulfillment section, setting up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the word 'ככה' in the command section taught עיכובא, meaning that if the detail is missing, the inauguration does not work. But that word only covers what is written in that section (ספר שמות פרק כט). Some details appear only in the fulfillment section (ספר ויקרא פרק ח), so they need their own source.

keyTerms.meaning: a matter, a detail
the section or topic, here the Torah section about the מילואים
from where do we know it?
the seven-day inauguration of אהרן and his sons as כהנים

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'this section' means the command section in ספר שמות. The details that are 'not written in this section' are still written in the Torah, just in the fulfillment section in ספר ויקרא.

phrases.english: A matter that is written in this section [is indispensable, fine].
phrases.notes: This points back to what we learned earlier from the word 'ככה'.

phrases.english: A matter that is not written in this section
phrases.notes: Details that show up only in ספר ויקרא.

phrases.english: from where do we know [that it is indispensable]?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילְּתָא דְּלָא כְּתִיבָא בְּהַאי עִנְיָנָא מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about 'ככה' teaching עיכובא for the command section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that details written only in the fulfillment section (ספר ויקרא) are also indispensable.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: a גזירה שוה from 'פתח'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק links the two sections through the word 'פתח', which appears in both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We learn it from 'פתח' and 'פתח'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers with a גזירה שוה. The word 'פתח' (the opening of the אהל מועד) appears in both the command section and the fulfillment section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the same word appears in both sections, the two sections are treated as one unit. The עיכובא rule from 'ככה' in the command section therefore carries over to the details in the fulfillment section.

keyTerms.meaning: he learns, he derives
opening, the entrance of the אהל מועד
a derivation based on the same word appearing in two places

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
One derives [it from] 'opening' and 'opening'.
phrases.notes: שמות כט:לב and ויקרא ח:לא both mention 'פתח אהל מועד'.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָלֵיף פֶּתַח פֶּתַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from 'פתח' joins both sections, so the עיכובא of the command section also applies to the fulfillment section.

steps.title: רב משרשיא: from 'Keep the charge of ה׳'
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא learns עיכובא directly from a verse in the fulfillment section itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: 'And you shall keep the charge of ה׳' teaches that it is indispensable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא offers a different source. He says the fulfillment section has its own verse that teaches עיכובא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No גזירה שוה is needed. The words 'ושמרתם את משמרת ה׳' (ויקרא ח:לה) appear right in the fulfillment section and stress strict guarding of the commands, which teaches that every detail there is indispensable.

keyTerms.meaning: and you shall guard or keep
a charge, a duty to be guarded
indispensable; if the detail is missing, the whole thing is invalid

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
'And you shall keep the charge of ה׳' teaches that it is indispensable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to step 1 that does not use the גזירה שוה of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase 'ושמרתם את משמרת ה׳' in the fulfillment section itself teaches עיכובא.

steps.title: רב אשי: from 'For so I am commanded'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי learns עיכובא from the next words in the same verse: 'כי כן צויתי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: 'For so I am commanded' teaches that it is indispensable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third source. He points to the closing words of the same verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כן' ('so', meaning exactly this way) works like 'ככה' in the command section. It shows that the details must be done exactly as described, so they are indispensable.

keyTerms.meaning: for so I have been commanded
so, in exactly this way

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
'For so I am commanded' teaches that it is indispensable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third alternative answer to step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כי כן צויתי' teaches עיכובא for the details in the fulfillment section.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three sources for עיכובא in the ספר ויקרא section: the גזירה שוה 'פתח פתח' (רב נחמן בר יצחק), 'ושמרתם את משמרת ה׳' (רב משרשיא), and 'כי כן צויתי' (רב אשי).

steps.title: A ברייתא lists three similar 'command' phrases
steps.stepSummary: Since רב אשי quoted 'כי כן צויתי', the גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists three similar phrases in the מילואים story.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'For so I am commanded', 'as I commanded', 'as ה׳ commanded'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The ברייתא lists three related phrases and then explains each one in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three phrases sound repetitive. The ברייתא assumes each one teaches something different, and the following steps say what each one adds.

keyTerms.meaning: as I commanded
as ה׳ commanded

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'For so I am commanded', 'as I commanded',
'as ה׳ commanded'.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Prompted by רב אשי's use of 'כי כן צויתי'; a side discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three similar phrases appear, and each teaches its own lesson.

steps.title: 'For so I am commanded': eat even while in mourning
steps.stepSummary: The first phrase teaches that the כהנים must eat the offering even in a state of אנינות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For so I am commanded' teaches that they must eat it even in a state of אנינות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the first phrase. משה told אהרן and his sons to eat the offering even though נדב ואביהוא had just died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an אונן, a mourner on the day of a close relative's death, may not eat קדשים. Here 'כי כן צויתי' teaches a special exception: during the מילואים, the כהנים had to eat even in אנינות.

keyTerms.meaning: the state of an אונן, a mourner on the day of a close relative's death
they shall eat it (the offering)

phrases.english: 'For so I am commanded': in a state of acute mourning they shall eat it.
phrases.notes: Said about the מנחה after the death of נדב ואביהוא.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי כֵן צֻוֵּיתִי בַּאֲנִינוּת יֹאכְלוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first phrase listed in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים ate the offering even while they were אוננים.

steps.title: 'As I commanded': told to them at the time of the event
steps.stepSummary: The second phrase shows that the instruction to eat in אנינות was given right at the time of the tragedy.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'As I commanded' means that he told them this at the time of the event.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the second phrase. משה is saying that he gave this instruction right then, at the time of the deaths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a time detail. The instruction to eat in אנינות was not an old general rule. It was told to them on the spot, right after נדב ואביהוא died.

keyTerms.meaning: at the time of the event

phrases.english: 'As I commanded':
he told them at the time of the event.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוֵּיתִי בִּשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה אָמַר לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second phrase listed in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The command to eat in אנינות was told to them at the moment of the event.

steps.title: 'As ה׳ commanded': not on my own authority
steps.stepSummary: The third phrase shows that משה was passing on ה׳'s command, not ruling on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'As ה׳ commanded' means: I am not saying this on my own.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the third phrase. משה stresses that the unusual instruction came from ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since eating קדשים in אנינות is normally forbidden, someone might think משה made a temporary ruling on his own. The phrase rules that out: this was a direct command from ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: on my own, by my own initiative

phrases.english: 'As ה׳ commanded':
and not on my own am I saying it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה׳ וְלֹא מֵאֵלַי אֲנִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third phrase and completes the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The instruction was ה׳'s command, not משה's own idea.
steps.whatToRemember: Each phrase adds something: 'כי כן צויתי' teaches eating in אנינות, 'כאשר צויתי' teaches that it was said at the time of the event, and 'כאשר צוה ה׳' teaches that it came from ה׳.

steps.title: Trousers and the tenth of an ephah are included by 'וזה'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא teaches that the מכנסים and the עשירית האיפה, which are not written in the section, are included through 'וזה הדבר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: The trousers are not written in the section. When it says 'And this is the thing that you shall do to them to sanctify them to serve Me', this comes to include the trousers and the tenth of an ephah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the theme of details that are not written in the section. רבי יוסי בר חנינא shows how two missing items are still included in the מילואים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מכנסים are not listed among the clothes in the מילואים section. The extra 'ו' in 'וזה' (שמות כט:א) adds to what is written, bringing in the מכנסים and the עשירית האיפה (the מנחת חינוך, the meal offering a כהן brings when he begins to serve).

keyTerms.meaning: the trousers of the כהן
in the Torah section
to include
a tenth of an ephah of flour, the meal offering brought when a כהן begins to serve

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even items not stated outright can be part of the מילואים through a hint in the verse. This links back to the question of unwritten details in step 1.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
Trousers are not written in the section;
when it says: 'And this is the thing
phrases.notes: שמות כט:א. The extra 'ו' ('and') is what adds something more.

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה לָהֶם לְקַדֵּשׁ אֹתָם לְכַהֵן״ —
phrases.english: that you shall do to them to sanctify them to serve as priests',
phrases.notes: The verse also says 'לי' (to Me), but the quote here leaves it out.

phrases.english: this comes to include the trousers and the tenth of an ephah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא מִכְנָסַיִם אֵין כְּתוּבִין בַּפָּרָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side discussion of the three phrases to the topic of details not written in the section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra 'ו' of 'וזה' includes the מכנסים and the עשירית האיפה in the מילואים.

steps.title: Where do we learn the tenth of an ephah?
steps.stepSummary: The מכנסים are understandable because they appear in the section about the בגדים, but what is the source for the עשירית האיפה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the trousers are written in the section about the garments. But the tenth of an ephah, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks back at רבי יוסי בר חנינא's teaching and accepts half of it, the מכנסים. It then asks for a source for the other half, the עשירית האיפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מכנסים are mentioned near the מילואים section, in the section about the בגדי כהונה, so 'וזה הדבר' can reasonably include them. The עשירית האיפה has no such nearby mention, so the גמרא wants to know what links it to the מילואים.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this part is fine
The trousers of the כהן
A tenth of an ephah of flour, a מנחה offering
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Granted, the trousers
are written in the section about the garments,
but the tenth of an ephah, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא מִכְנָסַיִם כְּתִיבִי בְּעִנְיָנָא דִבְגָדִים, אֶלָּא עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source for one half of רבי יוסי בר חנינא's teaching
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What links the עשירית האיפה to the מילואים section?

steps.title: Learned from the word 'this' in both places
steps.stepSummary: The עשירית האיפה is learned through a גזירה שוה from the word 'זה', which appears both in the מנחה verse and in the מילואים verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from 'this' and 'this': from the verse 'And this is the offering of אהרן and his sons which they shall offer to ה׳, a tenth of an ephah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'זה' links the two פסוקים. Because of that link, the עשירית האיפה becomes part of the מילואים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מילואים verse says 'וזה הדבר', and the מנחה verse says 'וזה קרבן אהרן ובניו... עשירית האיפה'. The shared word 'זה' acts as a גזירה שוה, carrying the עשירית האיפה over into the מילואים requirements.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes / it is derived (often through a גזירה שוה)
The shared word 'this' that connects the two verses
A link between two verses that use the same word

phrases.english: It is derived from 'this' and 'this'
from 'And this is the offering of Aaron and his sons'
which they shall offer to ה׳
a tenth of an ephah.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָתְיָא ״זֶה״ ״זֶה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from 'זה' in וזה קרבן אהרן to 'וזה הדבר' of the מילואים
steps.whatToRemember: Both the מכנסים and the עשירית האיפה are included in the מילואים through 'וזה הדבר'. The מכנסים come in because they are nearby in the garments section, and the עשירית האיפה comes in through a גזירה שוה of 'זה'.

steps.title: Even reading the section aloud is required
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, teaches that if משה had not read the מילואים פרשה aloud to the people, the מילואים would not have been valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: From where do we know that even reading the section is required? The verse says, 'And משה said to the congregation: This is the thing that ה׳ commanded.' Even the speaking is required.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching is added: besides the actions, saying the פרשה aloud to the people was also an essential part of the מילואים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse records that משה spoke to the עדה before acting. רשב"י reads 'הדבר' as hinting to 'דיבור', speech, so the speaking itself becomes a required step and not just an introduction.

keyTerms.meaning: Reading the Torah section aloud
Holds back / without it the process is not valid
The verse teaches
Speech / the spoken part

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that in the מילואים even a spoken, non-physical part was considered essential.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
From where do we know that even reading the section is required (invalidates if missing)?
The verse says: 'And Moshe said to the congregation:
This is the thing that ה׳ commanded' —
even the speaking is required.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי: מִנַּיִין שֶׁאַף מִקְרָא פָּרָשָׁה מְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another indispensable element of the מילואים, learned from a different verse that also uses the phrase 'זה הדבר' (ויקרא ח:ה, not שמות כט:א)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading the מילואים פרשה aloud was essential (מעכב)

steps.title: How did משה dress them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic: in what order did משה dress אהרן and his sons in the בגדי כהונה?
steps.simpleTranslation: How did he dress them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question about the order of dressing during the מילואים. This sets up the back-and-forth that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about order: did משה dress אהרן first, or everyone together? The next steps will test whether this question is even worth asking.

keyTerms.meaning: How / in what way
He dressed them

phrases.english: How did he dress them?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד הִלְבִּישָׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic arising from the מילואים discussion
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The order in which משה dressed אהרן and his sons

steps.title: Why ask about the past?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the question has no practical point, because whatever happened already happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did he dress them?! What was, was!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own question: knowing the order of a one-time past event changes nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants its questions to have a purpose. A purely historical detail with no practical result is called 'מאי דהוה הוה', what happened, happened.

keyTerms.meaning: What was, was (a past event with no practical relevance)

phrases.english: How did he dress them?!
What was, was!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דַהֲוָה הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the usefulness of the question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A past event that will never repeat has no practical result
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is repeating its own words here as a challenge, not asking the question a second time. The '?!' means 'Why would you even ask this?'

steps.title: Maybe it means in the future
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the question is really about how the כהנים will be dressed in the future, when the עבודה returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: how will he dress them in the future to come?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to rescue the question by giving it a practical purpose: preparing for the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the dressing will happen again לעתיד לבוא, then knowing the order matters. That would answer the objection that 'what was, was'.

keyTerms.meaning: In the future to come (the time of the redemption / תחיית המתים)
He will dress them / dresses them

phrases.english: Rather: how will he dress them in the future to come?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כֵּיצַד מַלְבִּישָׁן לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reframes the question to answer the objection
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about a past event and therefore pointless
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about future practice

steps.title: In the future, משה will be there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the future-based reading, because משה himself will be there and will know what to do.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the future too, when אהרן and his sons come, and משה will be with them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion from step 15: there is no need to work this out now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לעתיד לבוא, אהרן, his sons, and משה will all return. משה will simply know the right order, so studying it now for that reason accomplishes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Also / too
When they will come

phrases.english: In the future to come also,
when Aaron and his sons come, Moshe will be with them!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא נָמֵי, לִכְשֶׁיָּבוֹאוּ אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו וּמֹשֶׁה עִמָּהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reframing of step 15
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The future-practice reading of the question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: משה will be present and will know the order himself

steps.title: The question is about understanding the verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles on the purpose of the question: to understand the פסוקים correctly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: how did he dress them? In order to understand the verses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final reason the question is worth asking: the goal is to explain the פסוקים, which seem to describe the dressing in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even without a practical result, learning to read the Torah's verses correctly is a valid goal. That is why the original question about the past is allowed after all.

keyTerms.meaning: To understand / explain the verses

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a general rule: understanding the Torah text is a good enough reason to ask a question, even when no practical law depends on it.

phrases.english: Rather: how did he dress them?
In order to understand the verses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כֵּיצַד הִלְבִּישָׁן לְמִיסְבַּר קְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new justification after step 16 rejected the previous one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the purpose of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A question needs a practical result to be worth asking
steps.terutzMaskana: Understanding the verses is purpose enough

steps.title: A dispute about the order of dressing
steps.stepSummary: The sons of רבי חייא and רבי יוחנן disagree. One says אהרן was dressed first and then his sons; the other says אהרן and his sons were dressed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons of רבי חייא and רבי יוחנן disagree about this. One said: אהרן, and afterward his sons. And one said: אהרן and his sons at once.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the question is justified, the גמרא brings two opinions on how משה dressed the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One opinion holds that משה fully dressed אהרן before starting on his sons. The other holds that he dressed them all in one continuous process, so as to keep the order of garments written in the פסוקים. The next part of the גמרא will explain how each opinion reads the verses.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree
The sons of רבי חייא (יהודה and חזקיה)
At once / together, without a break

steps.confusionAlert: 'בבת אחת' does not mean everyone was dressed in the exact same instant. It means they were dressed together in one continuous flow, one after another, without stopping.

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בָּהּ בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן.
phrases.english: The sons of Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Yochanan disagree about this.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: אַהֲרֹן וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּנָיו,
phrases.english: One said: Aaron, and afterward his sons;

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו בְּבַת אַחַת.
phrases.english: and one said: Aaron and his sons at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בָּהּ בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the now-justified question of how משה dressed them
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: אהרן first and then his sons, or אהרן and his sons together

steps.title: אביי limits the dispute to the belt
steps.stepSummary: אביי says everyone agrees that אהרן was dressed first in the כתונת and מצנפת. The argument is only about the אבנט.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: For the tunic and the turban, everyone agrees that אהרן was dressed first and then his sons. In both the command section and the doing section, אהרן is mentioned first. Where they argue is about the belt.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shrinks the argument from Step 18. He says it is not about all the בגדים, only about the אבנט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה describes the dressing twice: once as a command (צוואה, in שמות) and once as it actually happened (עשייה, in ויקרא). For the כתונת and מצנפת, both sections mention אהרן before his sons, so no one can argue. The אבנט is different, which sets up the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The tunic, a long shirt-like garment
The turban / head covering
Everyone agrees (literally: the whole world does not argue)
Command: the section where ה׳ tells משה what to do
Doing: the section describing what משה actually did
The belt / sash

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אביי is taking a side in the argument. He is only pointing out where the argument really is: just the אבנט.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic גמרא move: narrowing a broad dispute down to the one point where the sources actually conflict.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
With the tunic and the turban
everyone agrees
that it was Aharon first and afterward his sons.
For both in the command and in the doing
phrases.notes: צוואה = שמות כט; עשייה = ויקרא ח

phrases.english: Aharon comes first.
Where they argue is about the belt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בְּכֻתּוֹנֶת וּמִצְנֶפֶת כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact scope of the dispute from Step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For כתונת and מצנפת, אהרן was dressed first by everyone's view; the dispute is only about the אבנט.

steps.title: Source for the view that אהרן was belted first
steps.stepSummary: The view that אהרן came first learns it from the doing section, where אהרן is belted, and only later his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says אהרן first and then his sons learns it from what is written: 'He girded him with the belt,' and only afterward is it written: 'He girded them with belts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the פסוק behind the first opinion: אהרן first, then his sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא ח:ז, משה belts אהרן ('אותו', him). Only later, in ח:יג, does משה belt the sons ('אותם', them). The order of the פסוקים shows two separate belting moments, אהרן first.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (introducing an opinion)
And he girded him (one person: אהרן)
And afterward it is written

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר אַהֲרֹן וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּנָיו,
phrases.english: The one who says Aharon and afterward his sons,
because it is written: 'And he girded him with the belt,'
and then it is written: 'And he girded them with belts.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר אַהֲרֹן וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּנָיו, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק for the first side of the dispute over the אבנט
steps.raayaObject: The view that אהרן was belted before his sons
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא ח:ז and ח:יג: two separate belting verses, אהרן first

steps.title: Source for the view that they were belted together
steps.stepSummary: The view that אהרן and his sons were belted together learns it from the command section, which uses one phrase for all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says אהרן and his sons were done at once learns it from what is written: 'And you shall gird them,' meaning all of them together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the פסוק behind the second opinion: אהרן and his sons were belted together in one continuous act, without a break between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the command section (שמות כט:ט) the תורה says 'וחגרת אותם אבנט אהרן ובניו', putting אהרן and his sons together in one act. This view reads that as belting them all together in one continuous act, one after another without a break.

keyTerms.meaning: At once, simultaneously
And you shall gird them (all of them, in the command)

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו בְּבַת אַחַת,
phrases.english: And the one who says Aharon and his sons at once,
because it is written: 'And you shall gird them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו בְּבַת אַחַת, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק for the second side of the dispute
steps.raayaObject: The view that אהרן and his sons were belted simultaneously
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות כט:ט: one command covering אהרן and his sons together

steps.title: Challenge to the together view from the doing section
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to the together view, what about the doing section, where אהרן is belted first and his sons later?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says אהרן and his sons were done at once, isn't it written: 'He girded him with the belt,' and then it is written: 'He girded them with belts'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'together' opinion with the same פסוקים the first opinion used. The answer will come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'together' view relies on the command section. But the doing section clearly describes two separate beltings, אהרן first. So how can this view explain the order in ויקרא?

keyTerms.meaning: And according to the one who says
But isn't it written? (introduces a challenge from a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion. The גמרא is reusing the פסוקים from Step 20 to question the other side.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו בְּבַת אַחַת,
phrases.english: And according to the one who says Aharon and his sons at once,
isn't it written: 'And he girded him with the belt'
and then it is written: 'And he girded them with belts'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו בְּבַת אַחַת, הָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source from Step 20 to challenge the view in Step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that אהרן and his sons were belted simultaneously
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ויקרא ח describes two separate belting acts, אהרן ('אותו') and later the sons ('אותם'), which contradicts belting them all at once.
